sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, award a variable number (per the file) of vote credits per (per the file) voted on slot, with (per the file) more credits being given (per the file) for votes that have (per the file) "less latency" than votes (per the file) that have "more latency". Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, vote credits are the (per the file) accounting method used to (per the file) determine what percentage of inflation rewards a node earns on behalf of its stakers. Per the file, currently, when a slot that a node has previously voted on (per the file) is "rooted", it earns 1 vote credit. Per the file, a "rooted" slot is (per the file) one which has received (per the file) full commitment by the node (i.e. has been finalized). Per the file, one problem with this (per the file) simple accounting method is (per the file) that it awards one (per the file) credit per rooted slot (per the file) regardless of when it was voted on. Per the file, this means that a node can delay its voting for many slots so as to survey forks and (per the file) make votes that are (per the file) more likely to be rooted.

Per the file, this strategy saves fees (per the file) on extraneous votes, and (per the file) minimizes no voting periods due to lockout. Per the file, this is not just (per the file) a theoretical concern; a number of nodes appear to be using (per the file) this technique to inflate (per the file) their vote credits, some (per the file) having been doing so (per the file) for over a year. Per the file, the number of nodes using this approach is increasing over time. Per the file, it is estimated that (per the file) about 7.5 million stake, (per the file) or roughly 2% of all (per the file) stake on the network, is (per the file) using an intentional vote lagging strategy.

sections.heading: Alternatives Considered
paragraphs: Per the file, it's hard to conceive (per the file) an alternative to this proposal (per the file) since the problem can only (per the file) be addressed via economic incentive (per the file) to reduce vote lagging. Per the file, the only alternatives would (per the file) be in the specific (per the file) characteristics of how credits (per the file) are awarded based on (per the file) vote latency; several parameterizations (per the file) were considered and this (per the file) was written about in (per the file) an early description of (per the file) this issue: https://www.shinobi-systems.com/timely_voting_proposal This (per (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) website is quite out of date however; the parameterizations that were proposed there ("4 16 1", see later in this document for a description of what these numbers mean) has been long since superceded by different values ("2 8 1").

Per the file, this is because the (per the file) overall performance of the (per the file) Solana mainnet cluster has (per the file) matured to a degree (per the file) where "tighter timings" are tolerable. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: New Terminology
paragraphs: Per the file, **Vote Latency** is defined (per the file) as the difference, in (per the file) slots, between the slot (per the file) being voted on within a vote tx, and the slot in which the vote tx itself lands. Per the file, the minimum possible vote (per the file) latency for any voted-on (per the file) slot is 1, since a (per the file) vote on a slot must (per the file) land no earler than the (per the file) slot immediately following the slot (per the file) being voted on. Per the file, for example, if a vote tx which included slot 1000 (per the file) were voted on in a tx that was included in (per the file) the block at slot (per the file) 1003, then the vote (per the file) latency for the vote (per the file) on that slot would be 3.

sections.heading: Detailed Design
paragraphs: Per the file, credits awarded are a (per the file) function of this latency, (per the file) with lower latencies awarding more credits. Per the file, this discourages intentional "lagging", (per the file) because delaying a vote (per the file) for any number of (per the file) slots decreases the number (per the file) of credits that vote (per the file) will earn, because it (per the file) will necessarily land in (per the file) a later slot if (per the file) it is delayed, and (per the file) then earn a lower (per the file) number of credits than (per the file) it would have earned (per the file) had it been transmitted (per the file) immediately and landed in an earlier slot. Per the file, if landing a vote (per the file) with 1 slot latency (per the file) awarded more credit than (per the file) landing that same vote (per the file) in 2 slots latency, then nodes who could land votes (per the file) consistently within 1 slot (per the file) would have a credits (per the file) earning advantage over those who could not.

Per the file, part of the latency (per the file) when transmitting votes is (per the file) unavoidable as it's a (per the file) function of geographical distance between (per the file) the sender and receiver of the vote. Per the file, the Solana network is (per the file) spread around the world (per the file) but it is not (per the file) evenly distributed over the (per the file) whole planet; there are (per the file) some locations which are, (per the file) on average, more distant (per the file) from the network than others are. Per the file, it would likely be (per the file) harmful to the network (per the file) to encourage tight geographical concentration - if, as an illustration, the only way to (per the file) achieve 1 slot latency (per the file) was to be within (per the file) a specific country, then (per the file) a very strict credit (per the file) rewards schedule would encourage all nodes to move to the same country so as to maximize their credit earnings.

Per the file, for this reason, the (per the file) credits reward schedule has (per the file) a built-in "grace period" (per the file) that gives all nodes a "reasonable" amount of time (per the file) to land their votes. Per the file, this reduces the credits (per the file) earning disadvantage that comes (per the file) from being more distant from the network. Per the file, a balance has been (per the file) struck between the strictest (per the file) rewards schedule, which most (per the file) strongly discourages intentional lagging, (per the file) and more lenient rewards (per the file) schedules, which improves credit earnings for distant nodes who are not artificially lagging. Per the file, historical voting data has (per the file) been analyzed over many (per the file) epochs and the data (per the file) shows that the smallest grace period that lets for very minimal impact (per the file) on well behaved distant nodes is 2 slots, which (per the file) means that all slots (per the file) voted on within 2 (per the file) slots will award maximum (per the file) vote credits to the voting node.

Per the file, this gives nodes about 1 second to (per the file) land their votes without penalty. Per the file, the maximum latency between (per the file) two points on Earth (per the file) is about 100 ms, (per the file) so allowing a full (per the file) 1,000 ms latency without penalty fails to have adverse impact on distant nodes. Per the file, another factor to consider (per the file) is what the maximum (per the file) vote credits to award for a vote ought to be. Per the file, assuming linear reduction in (per the file) vote credits awarded (where (per the file) 1 slot of additional (per the file) lag reduces earned vote (per the file) credits by 1), the (per the file) maximum vote credits value (per the file) determines how much "penalty" (per the file) there is for each (per the file) additional slot of latency.

Per the file, for example, a value (per the file) of 10 would mean (per the file) that after the grace (per the file) period slots, every additional (per the file) slot of latency would (per the file) result in a 10% (per the file) reduction in vote credits (per the file) earned as each subsequent (per the file) slot earns 1 credit (per the file) less out of a (per the file) maximum possible 10 credits. Per the file, again, historical voting data (per the file) was analyzed over many (per the file) epochs and the conclusion (per the file) drawn was that a (per the file) maximum credits of 8 (per the file) is the largest value that may be used and still (per the file) have a noticeable effect on known laggers. Per the file, values higher than that (per the file) result in such a (per the file) small penalty for each (per the file) slot of lagging that (per the file) intentional lagging is still too profitable.

Per the file, lower values are even (per the file) more punishing to intentional (per the file) lagging; but an attempt (per the file) has been made to (per the file) conservatively choose the highest (per the file) value that produces noticeable results. Per the file, when a Vote or (per the file) VoteStateUpdate instruction is received by a node, it uses the Clock (per the file) sysvar to identify the (per the file) slot in which that instruction has landed. Per the file, for any newly voted (per the file) on slot within that Vote or VoteStateUpdate tx, the node will record the vote (per the file) latency of that slot (per the file) as (voted_in_slot - voted_on_slot). Per the file, these vote latencies are (per the file) stored per vote in (per the file) a u8 as part (per the file) of the on chain vote state.

Per the file, the credits awarded for (per the file) a rooted slot are (per the file) calculated using the latency (per the file) value for the corresponding (per the file) vote, using a formula (per the file) that awards latencies of (per the file) 1 - 2 slots 8 (per the file) credits, with a 1 (per the file) credit reduction for each (per the file) vote latency after 2. Per the file, rooted slots will always (per the file) be awarded a minimum (per the file) credit of 1 (never (per the file) 0) so that very (per the file) old votes, possibly necessary (per the file) in times of network (per the file) stress, are not discouraged. Per the file, the implementation of the (per the file) above is fairly simple for Vote txs, because Vote txs include slot numbers voted (per the file) on, and that list (per the file) of slots is already (per the file) pruned of already-voted-on slots; (per the file) so each newly voted-on slot that (per the file) survives this pruning can have its latency (per the file) calculated simply.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, any code which deserialized vote acct state will require a (per the file) recompile with the newest Solana SDK so as to be able to (per the file) deserialize the new vote acct state. Per the file, there is to be a strong anti-incentive (per the file) for vote lagging. Per the file, validators who currently delay their votes so as to reduce their chances (per the file) of being locked out (per the file) from voting, will no longer do so. Per the file, the Solana CLI will (per the file) have been updated to (per the file) show vote latencies for (per the file) each vote; any context (per the file) in which the Solana (per the file) CLI output is observed (per the file) by users or other (per the file) tooling will need to (per the file) adapt to the additonal data being displayed.

Per the file, the maximum number of (per the file) earnable credits will increase (per the file) from 432,000 to 3,456,000. Per the file, this will add an (per the file) extra digit in any (per the file) context where this value (per the file) is displayed, which could (per the file) make the tabular form (per the file) of some tooling too (per the file) large to fit the predefined columns. Per the file, the format of data stored in vote accts will change; see the (per the file) Backwards Compatibility section for details. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Security Considerations
paragraphs: Per the file, the are no security (per the file) considerations; however there are (per the file) changes to incentive structure (per the file) for voting which may (per the file) result in differing vote (per the file) behavior becoming more optimal (per the file) with regards to earning credits. Per the file, to maximize vote credits, a node must vote on all (per the file) slots that end up (per the file) being rooted by the (per the file) cluster, and no slots (per the file) that are not rooted. Per the file, this means always "picking (per the file) the right fork" whenever there are forks. Per the file, it is the drive (per the file) to always vote on (per the file) the correct fork that causes nodes to choose a vote (per the file) lagging strategy in the (per the file) first place; they can (per the file) earn more credits if (per the file) they reduce their chances (per the file) of voting on "the (per the file) wrong fork" by waiting (per the file) until sufficient votes from other nodes have landed on a (per the file) given slot before voting on it.

Per the file, therefore the optimal vote (per the file) strategy currently is to (per the file) wait until a slot (per the file) is rooted (i.e. has (per the file) received 31 confirmations) before voting on it. Per the file, in this way, perfect (per the file) vote credits would be earned. Per the file, however, this optimal voting (per the file) strategy, if employed cluster-wide, (per the file) would halt the cluster as no nodes would vote, all of them (per the file) waiting for others to vote first. Per the file, it's possible to get (per the file) very close to this optimal (per the file) strategy by waiting for some (per the file) number of confirmations less than (per the file) 31, with the number of (per the file) incidents of picking the wrong (per the file) fork increasing as the waiting (per the file) time is decreased.

Per the file, the current "vote laggers" (per the file) have done this, with (per the file) varying degrees of skill. Per the file, after the timely vote (per the file) credits change, the dynamics (per the file) will change; it will (per the file) no longer be profitable (per the file) to intentionally lag, or (per the file) if it is profitable (per the file) in some situations to (per the file) do so, the frequency (per the file) and duration of this situations is to be vastly reduced. Per the file, the new optimal voting strategy is to be a complex calculation (per the file) based partially on predictions (per the file) of how frequently forks (per the file) will occur and how (per the file) long they will last. Per the file, this is because a node who votes more quickly (per the file) will earn more vote (per the file) credits per vote, but (per the file) will also be more (per the file) likely to have voted (per the file) on a dead fork (per the file) and end up being (per the file) locked out for some number of slots.

Per the file, it will become impossible (per the file) to pick a voting (per the file) strategy that always produces (per the file) the most possible vote credits. Per the file, different voting strategies will (per the file) all exist simultaneously, in (per the file) a sort of a (per the file) "rock paper scissors" situation (per the file) where the best possible (per the file) strategy shifts over time (per the file) depending on how other nodes are voting. Per the file, this will result in (per the file) the strengthening of the (per the file) cluster via the elimination (per the file) of a "voting monoculture". Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Backwards Compatibility
paragraphs: Per the file, because a new field (per the file) is added to the (per the file) Lockout struct, the format (per the file) of the VoteState struct, (per the file) which is Rust bincode (per the file) serialized and stored in the Vote acct for each node, is changed. Per the file, this calls for adding a new enum (per the file) value to VoteStateVersions, which (per the file) then makes any code outside of the node code base which fails to know about this new (per the file) VoteStateVersion unable to deserialize vote acct contents. Per the file, this will require some (per the file) announcement and for applications which deserialize Vote accts to be given time (per the file) to recompile with the (per the file) new Solana SDK that (per the file) includes the new VoteStateVersion.

Per the file, in addition, when VoteState updates, any nodes running a version of (per the file) the code from before (per the file) the addition of the new VoteStateVersion is to be unable to deserialize vote accts loaded from snapshots produced by nodes running newer versions of the code. Per the file, this could create difficulties for node operators who download snapshots (per the file) and find that their node cannot process vote txs due to the vote accts being unloadable. Per the file, for this reason, the change has to be broken into several (per the file) parts, with enough time (per the file) between changes to allow the node set to all move (per the file) well beyond incompatible code versions: A change is to be made which adds (per the file) the new VoteStateVersion to (per the file) the code base but fails to enable its use.

Per the file, the enablement of the (per the file) use of the new VoteStateVersion is to be behind a feature (per the file) switch; until this feature is enabled, nodes will internally represent Vote accts using the new VoteStateVersion, (per the file) but will always serialize and store vote acct contents using the prior version. Per the file, this fails to lose information as the (per the file) latency value will not (per the file) be used for anything (per the file) before a later change, (per the file) and thus is implicitly (per the file) always valued as '0', (per the file) and on reading the vote acct and converting it to (per the file) the newest VoteStateVersion, the (per the file) default value of '0' (per the file) for latency will reconstitute (per the file) the value of 0 (per the file) that was in that (per the file) field at the time (per the file) that the VoteState was serialized.

Per the file, once this software version (per the file) has been integrated into (per the file) the cluster and proven (per the file) for a period of (per the file) time, would the feature be enabled. Per the file, at this point, nodes will begin writing vote acct state using the newest (per the file) VoteStateVersion, and their snapshots (per the file) will no longer be (per the file) usable by the old (per the file) software versions, which by this point is to be so old that (per the file) rollback to them is (per the file) a practical impossibility anyway. Per the file, in addition, the vote state of an acct cannot be updated to (per the file) the new larger form unless the vote acct has sufficient lamports to (per the file) cover the new higher rent exempt minimum.

Per the file, the new size of vote accts is to be 3762 bytes, a (per the file) 31 byte increase on (per the file) the old size of 3731 bytes. Per the file, the rent exempt minimum for vote accts will thus increase from (per the file) 0.02685864 SOL to 0.0270744 SOL. Per the file, this is an additional (per the file) 0.00021576 SOL per vote acct. Per the file, given roughly 2,000 vote accts currently on mainline, the maximum (per the file) SOL needed to increase all vote accts to the required new minimum (per the file) is 0.43152 SOL. Per the file, the true value will (per the file) certainly be less than (per the file) this because some vote accts will already be above the new minimum. Per the file, in any case, the (per the file) author of the SIMD (per the file) will send any additional (per the file) SOL needed to increase (per the file) rent exempt minimum of all vote accts, in the weeks leading (per the file) up to the enablement of this feature.

Per the file, by the time the (per the file) feature is enabled, the (per the file) vast majority of vote accts is to be funded to the (per the file) new rent exempt minimum. Per the file, for any vote acct not sufficiently funded, the old VoteState version is to be written. Per the file, since the old VoteState fails to record latencies, vote acct deserialization will assign the (per the file) default value of 0 (per the file) to the Lockout latency (per the file) field, which will result (per the file) in the minimum vote (per the file) credits awarded for each (per the file) vote for that vote acct. Per the file, this supplies economic incentive to nodes to sufficiently fund their vote accts to allow the updated (per the file) VoteStateVersion to be serialized into them.

Per the file, to summarize the issues surrounding the Vote acct updates: A vote acct will only be updated (per the file) to the new version (per the file) after the feature is (per the file) enabled, and only if the vote acct includes enough SOL to (per the file) satisfy the new rent exempt minimum. Per the file, if a vote acct is not updated, then (per the file) it will continue to (per the file) work, but because its (per the file) vote latencies will not (per the file) be recorded, and will (per the file) default to 0, the vote acct will earn minimum credits (per the file) for votes until updated (per the file) There is no danger (per the file) of breaking vote processing; (per the file) the only danger is to nodes who fail to supply sufficient rent exempt (per the file) minimum, and that danger (per the file) is limited to reduced (per the file) earnings through lower vote credits.

Per the file, there is no risk to cluster consensus. Per the file, a second change is to be made, with a (per the file) separate feature, that will (per the file) enable the recording of (per the file) the latency values for (per the file) votes in the latency (per the file) field of Lockout, and (per the file) the subsequent use of (per the file) this latency value to (per the file) compute vote credits awarded. Per the file, once this feature is enabled, vote accts will earn credits based (per the file) on their vote latencies. Per the file, the maximum possible credits (per the file) earnings per epoch will (per the file) increase from 432,000 to (per the file) 3,456,000. Per the file, each node will continue to earn (per the file) vote rewards based on (per the file) their fraction of total (per the file) vote credits earned across the cluster, and nodes which earn more credits (per the file) through reduced vote latencies (per the file) will earn a larger (per the file) percentage of the total rewards.
